1 · Key measures show what they are measured against

Pillar › Key measures

“the actual should show the proration like the performance”

Your row read 6# against 4# at 133%, and nothing on the slide said why. The missing number is the one Performance shows and the deck does not: what is due so far. It is already computed — §239 prorates a Sum measure — and the tactics table beside it has printed it since §252.

So the shape is one the deck already wears: the figure in bold, the benchmark quiet behind a slash. Nothing new is invented and no column is added.

Row 2 shows the rule working, not failing

Average sales compiles by Latest, which by your own decision does not prorate — a rate at a point in time is not a running total. So its benchmark is the full-year 6 M EGP, and the row above it, a Sum, is prorated to 3#. Two different numbers on one slide for the right reason.

Key Objectives — where we stand

Identical change, identical shape. Your Retail revenue row reads 3.59B EGP against 2.36B EGP at 99% — a number that only makes sense once the slide says the year-to-date target is 2.39B EGP.

3 · The doubled unit

Pillar › Key measures — row 2 of the shots above

“8MEGP is again is showing a gltich”

Nothing is doubling it now. I put every combination through the joiner and it never produces a repeat: what is stored on that row is already the string 8 M EGP M EGP, written before the joiner was corrected, and the slide is faithfully printing it. That residue was recorded at the time as the one case the fix could not reach — a value already stored doubled stays so until it is re-entered.

The proposed shot above already shows it healed. But where to heal it is your call, because the three answers differ in what they touch:

Which one?

A — heal it on screen. A unit repeated immediately is collapsed wherever a figure is drawn. Nothing stored changes, every surface reads right at once, and the workbook still carries the doubled string.
B — heal it on save. The next time anyone touches that figure it is written back clean. Correct at the source, and rows nobody re-enters stay wrong.
C — a migration. Every stored figure is swept once. It reaches everything including the workbook, and it rewrites data, which is the one thing this platform does not do lightly.
A and B are not exclusive, and doing both is what I would recommend.

4 · A tactic outside this cycle is not dimmed

Pillar › Tactics

“for a non due tactic don't dim it show it normally it has the comment of not due this cycle anyway”

Agreed, and it is one word removed. The row already says Outside this cycle in its own cell — dimming it says the same thing a second time in a way that also makes the owner and the quarters harder to read on a projector. Row 2 in the pair below.

5 · One cell was showing two different measures

Pillar › Tactics — YTD actual

“the ytd is showing 2% / 2# .. it's not 2% in the performance it's just 2 with a unit of #”

Reproduced exactly, and the cause is two questions where there should be one. The benchmark asks only whether the tactic has an outcome; the figure asks whether that outcome can be scored. A row whose outcome has a target but no figure yet answers yes to the first and no to the second — so the right-hand half reads the outcome's target (2#) while the left-hand half falls back to per-cent-delivered (2%). Two measures, one cell.

One question decides the whole cell: if the row is read on its outcome, both halves come from the outcome. A row that owes a figure then says so, in the words §252 already uses.

And one thing follows that I have not assumed

Progress still reads 4% on that row, from the fallback the figure was using. If the row is measured by its outcome and the outcome has not been reported, I would expect not scored rather than a number — the same rule the plan already applies to an unmeasured outcome. That changes a score, so it is yours to say.

7 · The pillars are named before they are scored

“before the pillars performance we need 1 slide with just the 2 titles … don't follow the same design but the concept of having the pillars first”

A roll-call: what this unit committed to, in its own words, before a single number. The concept is from your Raya deck; the treatment is the platform's own — no colour blocks, no invented 01 / 02 / 03.

The code is the number. RS01 is what every other surface calls that pillar, so it identifies the row and numbers it at the same time, where an invented 01 would only number it. Each pillar's own sub-line comes along where it has one.

It costs one slide and adds a place for a picture

The scoring table that exists today is unchanged and still follows. Every fixed slide is a place a picture can be inserted, so this one becomes a new position in Manage slides too — which is a gain, not a cost.

Shot at 1600×900 from the built platform, with your figures put into the demo so every row is real. Items 1, 2, 4 and 7 need only your yes; items 3, 5 and 6 carry a question I have not answered for you.
